To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) mutations in ion channel genes are a common cause of sudden cardiac death, and 2) mutations in ion channels can cause sudden death in the absence of other cardiac abnormalities.
The ion channel mutations that we have studied are responsible for the development of cardiac arrhythmias that can lead to sudden death.

mutations in the genes encoding the cardiac sodium channel (SCN5A) and the potassium channel KCNE2 (minK) are responsible for some forms of long QT syndrome (LQTS) and Brugada syndrome (BrS), respectively, which are both forms of sudden cardiac arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death (SCD).
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of cardiac arrhythmias in the context of the normal and diseased heart.
the identification of mutations in genes coding the ion channels that are responsible for cardiac arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.
the identification and characterization of mutations in genes encoding ion channel subunits that cause cardiac disorders, and with the elucidation of their functional consequences.

the ion channels, in particular the voltage-gated sodium and potassium channels, are involved in sudden cardiac death in the majority of cases.
the ion channelopathies are the most frequent and most important causes of sudden cardiac death, especially in young people.
mutations in the genes coding for ion channels, which are essential for cardiac function, are the most likely cause of sudden cardiac death.

we have shown that a single amino acid substitution can cause sudden cardiac death in humans.
mutations in ion channel genes are associated with sudden cardiac death in the absence of structural heart disease.
the mutations in the genes encoding ion channel subunits can result in a variety of cardiac arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.

there is a lot to be learned from studying the mechanisms of sudden cardiac death.
